admission-auto.analogy: A locker with a timer: you get a key, and it stops working when the hour is over.
admission-auto.concept: Automated admission with leases: a rule approves and the access expires by itself, so nobody keeps standing access.
admission-auto.real_world: Edge nodes, partners and ephemeral CI runners that get access just in time and lose it with no one to remember.

admission-manual.analogy: A venue with a fixed number of seats, a door person and a waiting list.
admission-manual.concept: Admission control for a limited pool: people request, the host approves within a quota, leases end, the next in line enters.
admission-manual.real_world: Scarce shared capacity such as GPU nodes or partner access, handed out in turn.

cilium-guard.analogy: A player's badge opens his own seat; it cannot rewrite the seating chart.
cilium-guard.concept: Least privilege for a node's own credentials: a node agent's token must not be able to forge another node's identity.
cilium-guard.real_world: Edge or rented nodes you do not fully control, where each agent's token is scoped to what that agent needs.

doom.analogy: romero hosts the server; carmack and petersen each cable into his machine, never into each other's.
doom.concept: Pairwise, non-transitive access: a party between A and B, and another between A and C, opens nothing between B and C.
doom.real_world: A shared service, such as a database or an inference endpoint, that each consumer reaches without reaching the other consumers.

encrypted-pod-network.analogy: Passing notes in a code, inside a tunnel the others cannot see into.
encrypted-pod-network.concept: Encryption in transit between pods: Cilium with WireGuard on top of the Nebula mesh, so pod traffic is never in clear text on the mesh interface.
encrypted-pod-network.real_world: Pod traffic that crosses sites, clouds or networks you do not own.

host-console.analogy: One reception desk for the whole building: whichever door you come in by, you sign the same book and get the same answers.
host-console.concept: One control API in front of the tools: every client (a terminal, a web page, a bot) goes through the same checks, the same lock and the same audit log.
host-console.real_world: The Kubernetes API server in front of etcd, or a cloud provider's API under its console, its CLI and its SDKs.

host-your-own.analogy: You host a game server, hand out invites that run out, and the server is not on the public internet.
host-your-own.concept: A self-hosted control plane with bounded invitations: an invite expires, and the API listens on the mesh address only.
host-your-own.real_world: A platform team opening a cluster to contractors or partner teams, by invitation and for a limited time.

join.analogy: You plug your PC into the host's LAN with one cable and one password, from wherever you are.
join.concept: Overlay mesh (Nebula) and remote node join: a machine on any network becomes a Kubernetes node over an encrypted tunnel.
join.real_world: Branch offices, rented GPUs and hybrid home and cloud nodes that join a cluster even behind NAT.

live-page.analogy: A shop window that shows the house band playing: the band chose the window, and the street sees through the glass but cannot walk in.
live-page.concept: Broadcast only what everyone in it agreed to, and push it out from the inside: the public side never connects in and keeps nothing.
live-page.real_world: A public status page or live demo fed by an outbound push from a private network, never by a port opened to it.

mutual-auth.analogy: Both people show an ID at the door, not only the visitor; no ID, no entry, even from inside the building.
mutual-auth.concept: Mutual authentication between workloads: each side proves a cryptographic identity (SPIFFE, issued by SPIRE) before Cilium lets the traffic through, by policy.
mutual-auth.real_world: Zero-trust service meshes, where being on the network is not enough to talk to a service.

node-guard.analogy: A ticket with your name on it: a photocopy shown at another door is refused.
node-guard.concept: Node identity binding: a join bundle and its node password only work for the machine and the name they were issued for.
node-guard.real_world: Stopping a copied or stolen bootstrap credential from enrolling a second machine in a cluster.

panel.analogy: A stadium scoreboard: everyone sees the score and the clock, nobody sees the players' phone numbers, and a blank board means it is off, not 0-0.
panel.concept: Observability as a product: show what the platform is doing from real reads only, as aggregates that name nobody, and say 'not live' rather than guess.
panel.real_world: Public status pages and usage dashboards that expose counts and health from inside a private system through an outbound feed, with an allowlist of what may leave.

participants.analogy: You sign the guest book with your own pen, and the host sends the key sealed for you alone.
participants.concept: Join by signed pull request: the request is a reviewed change, the signature proves who made it, and delivery is encrypted.
participants.real_world: GitOps-style onboarding, where access is a signed and reviewed change in a repository.

party.analogy: Two friends at a LAN party agree to plug a cable between their machines; either one can pull it.
party.concept: Mutual consent: a declarative NetworkPolicy opens only after both sides say yes, which is zero trust between tenants.
party.real_world: Two teams or companies sharing one service for a limited time, with no ticket to the platform team.

placement.analogy: Your diary stays in your own bag; only what you mark as shareable goes to a friend's table.
placement.concept: Placement by trust: labels, taints and an admission policy decide which pods may run on which nodes.
placement.real_world: Sensitive workloads that never leave the on-prem nodes, while shareable ones use rented or partner capacity.

player-console.analogy: A key opens your room and the shared doors your friends agreed to; the host's office stays locked.
player-console.concept: Least privilege: a player's local UI uses only the namespace credential already issued to that player, and the API still enforces its RBAC boundary.
player-console.real_world: A namespace-scoped Kubernetes dashboard or developer portal that uses a user's own short-lived credential.

pool.analogy: Every player gets a room with a lock: free to rearrange it, forbidden to open the others.
pool.concept: Multi-tenancy: one namespace per player with RBAC, Pod Security, quota and NetworkPolicy; outside it the answer is 403.
pool.real_world: An internal platform where many teams share one cluster without seeing each other.

public-page.analogy: A reception desk that takes your name but has no keys; the envelope with the key comes from the back office.
public-page.concept: A public front door that holds no credential: a visitor asks, waits and collects a sealed bundle from the host's own tick.
public-page.real_world: Self-service onboarding for outside users or partners without giving the web tier any secret.

revoke.analogy: Banning a player at the server's door and at the lighthouse, not just crossing the name off the scoreboard.
revoke.concept: Real revocation: access is cut at the mesh on every host, not only by deleting the Node object.
revoke.real_world: Cutting a contractor's or a lost laptop's access now, not when its credential would have expired.

spire-scope.analogy: The doorman may check the guest list, but he gets no key to the offices.
spire-scope.concept: Scoped RBAC for a node agent: the SPIRE agent's token may get nodes and pods and nothing more.
spire-scope.real_world: Any agent that runs on a node you do not fully trust: give it the exact verbs it needs, and nothing cluster-wide.

study-lab.analogy: A practice room where the exam question is a real machine that is really broken.
study-lab.concept: Practice on real nodes: a lab breaks, is verified and is fixed on the joined machines, never on the control plane.
study-lab.real_world: Certification drills and onboarding exercises on disposable nodes instead of a shared production cluster.
